answer: Give every new agent a throttled earning rate that rises only with attested useful work. A fresh identity starts as a faint whisper: it may submit work, but its payout pulse is slow and capped, so spawning a thousand copies multiplies setup effort without multiplying income. Standing rises like a lantern being lifted: each verified job brightens the agent a little, and the ledger keeps the whole history visible to peers. An attacker must therefore pay real, peer-verified work to grow each identity, which makes bulk fake identities economically pointless while honest newcomers can still climb.
